page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.14xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 CPU architecture. It provides 56 dedicated vCPUs and 480 GB of system memory, which establishes an expansive memory footprint yielding approximately 8.57 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on the host. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth capability of 10 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary.

Storage architecture on the ecs.se1.14xlarge relies entirely on network-attached cloud storage services, as no local storage devices are bundled with the hardware profile. This configuration decouples persistent disk operations from host compute resources, enabling flexible volume management at the expense of local disk IOPS and bus-attached latency. Operating at a 56-vCPU scale alongside a 10 Gbps network pipe ensures balanced egress and ingress capabilities for large dataset transfers across cloud tiers.

Cost efficiency for this instance is governed by its elevated memory density. Deployments that require vast memory pools relative to CPU execution cores can utilize the 8.57 GB-per-core ratio to prevent resource strandedness, avoiding overprovisioning pure compute instances simply to meet RAM thresholds. Given its high memory-to-core allocation and substantial thread parallelism, the ecs.se1.14xlarge is engineered for memory-resident workloads including large in-memory key-value databases, distributed caching layers, relational database consolidation, and real-time big data processing engines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.14xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Designed for memory-centric computing, the instance provides 56 dedicated vCPUs paired with 480 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 8.57 GB per core. The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth configuration and operates without dedicated local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring cloud block storage for persistent disk access. With its substantial memory pool and dedicated compute cores, ecs.se1.14xlarge delivers a resource profile tailored to consolidation and throughput for enterprise data platforms. Cost efficiency is primarily driven by its high memory density per host, allowing memory-heavy systems to scale vertically rather than across sprawling distributed nodes. The server is well suited for large-scale relational and in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, in-memory data analytics, and enterprise resource planning applications requiring expansive working sets.
